title: Be warned: Fallout 4's next update may break your mods - and there's a similar one for Skyrim in the works, too
author: Sherif Saed
content:
Rad medicine.

For most games, the news of a new patch is usually received with excitement. This is true for games made by Bethesda too, of course, but not when they're as old as Fallout 4 and Skyrim are. The reason? Mods.

Bethesda announced that a new update for Fallout 4 Creations (mods) will arrive today, 18th August to deliver "general improvements". In the patch's announcement on X, the developer advised players to log in and back up their save files, or manually save the load order of their mods before installing the patch as a precaution.

That's because, as anyone who plays the mod-friendly games of Bethesda knows, patches have a tendency to break mods. This is pretty typical, as mods are built to work with whatever version of the game was available when they were released. Even though patches may not directly alter some underlying feature a mod is built on, a new version number is enough to cause a disruption.

Again, this is nothing new for players who have been modding Bethesda games for years: the solution is for the mod's creator to release an updated version that works with the post-patch game, which is sometimes easier said than done when the creator has simply abandoned the project.

Players who run heavily modded versions of Bethesda's games typically use a series of interlocking and interdependent mods that alter the experience in major ways. When one breaks, any that depend on that mod to function will also cease to work. That can even have an effect on save files, which is why Bethesda is asking players to back theirs up just in case.

"Once your load order is saved, you'll be able to re-download your entire Creations list at once when the update is live," the developer added. Bethesda also confirmed that a similar Creations update is in the works for Skyrim, though did not offer a release date for that, promising to share details "soon".

As Bethesda takes its time working on The Elder Scrolls 6 and Fallout 5, mods have been offering a lifeline to sustain the Fallout 4 and Skyrim communities, even if they have to deal with this type of headache every once in a while.

title: Spider-Man is looking exceptionally strong in Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls, as he was in every top 8 team during the game's first major tournament
author: Connor Makar
content:
Hitting it out of the Parker.

Since its release, people have been throwing themselves at Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls. Much debate has been had around who are the strongest characters in the base roster, but now that the game's first big tournament has concluded, we may have an early answer.

Community Effort Orlando (CEO) was hosted over the weekend, and once again brought thousands of people to Florida to play a variety of fighting games. 1058 people entered the tournament bracket for Marvel Tōkon, giving us a great source of data for which characters are dominating in this early stage in the game's competitive life.

Of the top 8 players, every single one of them used Spider-Man in their team. Most used him as an assist character rather than as their starting fighter, though it's worth noting that tournament winning SonicFox had Spidey as their point character.

As for why Spider-Man proved so popular? Well, as a character he has a very strong offensive move list, and is able to open up blocking opponents with a variety of powerful blows. He's also in possession of one of the best overhead attacks in the game, which he can pull out quickly forcing you to quickly decide whether to block while standing or blocking.

There are some other characters worth looking at, though. Blade was present on six of the eight teams, and Magneto was present on five. Magik, who was the most popular character during the game's open beta, was the fourth most popular character and remains a strong contender on the roster, even if she has seemingly fallen by the wayside just a little.

The reaction to Spider-Man's popularity among the world's best Marvel Tōkon players has resulted in some to call for nerfs to hit the friendly neighborhood superhero, though it's also worth remembering that Marvel Tōkon hasn't been out for even a month yet. It's probably better to leave things as they are for a while longer, to see if Spider-Man and his peers present in top-tier teams remain there given additional scrutiny.

title: After a successful first week, Mistfall Hunter gets a roadmap promising a much requested solo mode for one of its maps
author: Oisin Kuhnke
content:
Let Me Solo This Map

Mistfall Hunter launched last week, and so far it seems to be doing quite well for itself! Apparently there's a million of you now running around its very Elden Ring looking lands and extraction fantasy lands (though these don't sound like one million sales, to be clear). With a healthy, if currently fairly critical, community under the game's belt, developer Bellring Games have shared a roadmap for its first and second season outlining what you can expect next.

The biggest thing, as addressed in this Steam blog post, is that after a lot of feedback, a solo mode is being introduced for both the normal and cataclysm difficulties of the Brandrgarde map. "That said, adding two new modes will inevitably split the matchmaking queue and present fresh class balance challenges in solo play," the devs note. "We'll continue to evaluate these factors and will communicate our findings with you before making further adjustments."

Then there's the three phases of season 1. In the first phase, an Einherjar mode is being added in, though details are slim on this. Seasonal tasks will also be introduced too, alongside the Soul Harvest, in which you can gather up soul cocoons, take on a (I think) boss called Soulgnawer, and take on a "multiplayer showdown." A special shop will let you gain special collectibles, soul coins, and moonlight nectar.

Phase two will bring with it the full roster of season tasks, allowing Pip to unlock the rare pouch and Nether Ferry skin. It's here where the solo mode for Brandrgarde will be added too, as well as an Underlord speed challenge where killing Underlords quickly gets you bonus rewards. Lastly, in phase three, a new monster called the Golden Woodling will be added in, a random match event dubbed Ancestor Tree can crop up, and completing certain tasks will tease aspects of season 2.

Speaking of season 2, a few details were shared for that. A new Blackarrow weapon, the javelin, will be added in for one. There'll be a new season to theme and "exclusive gameplay," as vague as that is, alongside a season-exclusive progression system. More details will be coming in time! You'll just have to be patient ya cheeky mist hunters.

title: Subnautica 2's Buddy System update brings in the promised proximity chat, easier trading, and emotes so you can sarcastically applaud your friends
author: Oisin Kuhnke
content:
What else would clapping be for?

Another month, another Subnautica 2 update! Last month's focus was on changing creature behaviours to make it a bit less frustrating for those of you that just wanted to go on a killing spree. This month puts the focus on your friends, with the 1.2 update being titled "Buddy System," adding in some neat new features that'll mean you'll have a smoother time playing with your pals.

For starters, the promised arrival of proximity chat is here. This works as you expect it to; while playing in multiplayer, friends sound louder when closer to you, and quieter when further away. What is quite a cute detail is the fact that the further away your friend gets, the more it sounds like it's coming over a radio signal that's losing reception. It's the small things!

On top of this there's a few other convenient bits related to multiplayer being added in. There'll now be player emotes, which are currently limited to thumbs upping or downing, clapping, raising your fists and clapping (you're encourage to use that one sarcastically when your friends biff it). Inventory sharing is a thing now too, just walk up to a friend and you can open up a menu that lets you directly move items between the two of you instead of having to drop things and pick them up.

Perhaps most usefully, if you or your friend gets downed for whatever reason, you'll have a short while to be able to swim up to them and share your oxygen to bring them back. And for customisation options, there's two new avatars to choose from to play as, and a couple more suit colours to choose from.

Some smaller additions include the arrival of a tracking tag that you can throw out into the environment to, well, track things. Alternatively you could pop one in a portable locker to make them easier to find if you have to leave it behind somewhere. If you have one on your person when you die, it'll also increase the range of your blackbox signal.

HUD icons will now be a lot smaller if you're not looking in their general direction, increasing in size if you are to make them easier to distinguish. Pinned recipes are seeing an improvement too, and the base builder tool should make it clearer when you can or can't place something. There'll be a range of bug fixes too, and the whole update is coming soon: tomorrow, August 19th. Happy subbing or whatever!

title: Amiga strategy classic Defender of the Crown is back with both old and fresh graphics, and an all new roguelite mode
author: Oisin Kuhnke
content:
As they say, the legend returns!

What's old is new (and also old) again! It's been 40 years since the release of the classic Amiga strategy game Defender of the Crown, and to mark the occasion it has received a new PC port called The Legend Returns that packages in the original game alongside a complete visual revamp and a totally fresh roguelike mode.

Defender of the Crown, for those unaware (and likely those under the age of 30) is a strategy game set in medieval England following the death of the king, prompting a range of factions to vie for control. Essentially your main goal is to build up a bigger army than anyone else, invade some castles, and occasionally do a bit of jousting. That's all there in The Legend Returns, complete with its original, pixelated Amiga graphics, but then there's also the new classic mode.

This one's essentially the same game, but with some modern graphics, "refined mechanics, and smoother systems." I'm actually quite pleased to see that visually, a lot of the game still uses pixel art, just with contemporary detail and flair. The jousting in particular looks really well realised, a satisfying approach to retaining the spirit of the original game while still providing the option of playing that version too.

And then, there's a totally new mode, the kingdom mode. This one mixes deckbuilding and dice-driven combat, meaning yes, it's a roguelite. Maps are procedurally generated in this mode, and you're tasked with "[uniting] the kingdom by defeating three enemy lords across a war-torn map, all while contending with brigands, rogues, and relentless Norman forces," as a press release explains. "Runs grow increasingly complex as players unlock new dice types, relics, and mechanics, while the world beyond the battlefield offers tournaments to enter, Saxon ladies to rescue, gold to raid, and castles to besiege."

Rescuing the Saxon ladies part is still a touch dated, so do take that with a pinch of salt. Otherwise, it's neat! You can pick it up on Steam right here.

title: Invisum Piscium 嫌魚 is a dreamlike walking sim about fragments of conversations and a deep craving for water fish haven't procreated in
author: Oisin Kuhnke
content:
You know, the regular stuff

I won't dive into why this is happening to me at the moment, you'll either need to pay me £20 or let me pay you to be my therapist to get that explanation, but I've been having some odd dreams lately. They're frequently temporally confused, mixing and matching people from across my life that should never have crossed paths. This has left me looking to ground myself a touch, so of course I decided to take a look at Invisum Piscium 嫌魚, a walking sim that's not quite about dreaming, but is about looking for distilled water that's free from fish sex contamination.

Invisum Piscium 嫌魚 is upfront about what it is on its Steam page. Atmosphere and exploration come first, there are "almost no traditional puzzle elements," you can pick up items and use them to "subtly alter the world." There's no question about this in the demo either. It opens in a bathroom, a rubber duck in front of you on the side of the bath. Of course you interact with the rubber duck, and it speaks back to you.

You leave the bathroom and find the main room in the apartment, a woman that looks like a plush doll brought to life starts talking to you about how she's losing her mind over the fact that fish mate in water, so she's feeling anxious about drinking it and asks for some distilled water. The quest begins! What follows in the demo, the process of getting to its ending (which does not see you acquire the distilled water) reminds me of the trading sequence in Link's Awakening, albeit in a smaller scale.

A depressed goth with a cat plush gives you a cake. She feels empty. You give the cake to a bunny girl, and she explodes and dies, so you bring her back to life with an energy drink. You find some money, so you buy a snack, and give it to the goth, and the exchange of miscellaneous goods continues. Ghosts float around the apartment complex you find yourself in with the goth and bunny girl, spouting cryptic messages. In the distance you can see the clouds, the corners of the skybox as clear as day and you wonder what the limits of this world are.

The demo for Invisum Piscium 嫌魚 isn't all that long, and it's not clear how big the full game would be. It certainly feels like it sits in conversation with indie classic Yume Nikki, and more recent games like nophenia. How far we'll all be lulled into its dreamlike world is a question that's yet to be answered. You can check out Invisum Piscium 嫌魚 for yourself on Steam.

title: Marble Souls dares to ask what would happen if the bloke from Dark Souls got stuck in a physics-driven ball, and it's out this year
author: Mark Warren
content:
Try rolling

FromSoft games famously often devolve into rolling around a big baddie. Marble Souls takes that a step further. Now, the rolling is the main event, not just a side effect of you not wanting to end up pancaked on the ground. You are a Dark Soulsy bloke in a Dark Soulsy world, but trapped inside a physics-driven ball and tasked with collecting lost souls. It looks cool.

— Stuffed Wombat (@stuffedwomb.at) 6 August 2026 at 15:00

Announced today, August 6th, by Mosa Lina publishers Stuffed Wombat, Marble Souls is set for release at some point before 2026 is out. "Instead of overcoming enemies, you'll be forging your way through an interconnected open world, upgrading your physics driven marble to suit your own personal playstyle," its devs wrote. "Mapping out your surroundings, collecting useful equipment and learning the ins and outs of your marble are not easy but Marble Souls is more about exploration and experimentation than rage-inducing progression loss."

As you go, you level up by collecting lost souls to upgrade your character's stats - which include the likes of accelerating, jumping, and rolling - and your marble itself. Rather than battling bosses, the challenge looks to be in finding shortcuts and opening up new routes to roll down.

Is it a funny premise that could wear out its welcome if the marble run isn't continually throwing up fresh twists and environments to negotiate? Maybe, but it certainly looks more thoughtfully-designed than a one-dimensional joke game. The music in the trailer also sounds cracking, the sort of mournfully beautiful tunes you need when you're doing your best impression of a medieval hamster.

If you fancy keeping tabs on Marble Souls as it rolls towards release, you can wishlist it on Steam.

title: Luigi Mangione pleads guilty to federal stalking charges and admits shooting UnitedHealthcare CEO
content:
News

Luigi Mangione pleads guilty to federal stalking charges and admits shooting UnitedHealthcare CEO

Luigi Mangione on Friday pleaded guilty to the two remaining charges against him in the death of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson in December 2024. The charges of interstate stalking resulting in death and stalking through use of interstate facilities resulting in death, filed in the US District Court for the Southern District of New York, both have a maximum penalty of life in prison without parole.

“I shot Mr. Thompson and he died. I knew what I was doing was illegal,” Mangione told the court during his allocution. He also said that he had never been treated or hospitalized for any mental illness or addiction, and that his mind was clear during the hearing.

Mangione does not have a plea deal with the federal government. Instead, he will face sentencing on December 18. Federal prosecutor Jamie McDonald said that the government would seek life imprisonment.

On January 30, Judge Margaret Garnett threw out two of the four charges against Mangione, including “murder through use of a firearm during and in relation to the stalking crimes charged…” A conviction on this charge would have made Mangione eligible for the death penalty.

Mangione still faces state charges in the case, scheduled for September 8. Mangione’s defense lawyer, Karen Friedman Agnifilo, filed a motion to dismiss the state’s second-degree murder and firearms charges, arguing a violation of due process and double jeopardy.

New York’s double jeopardy (when previous prosecution bars subsequent prosecution) statute is broader than the protection offered by the US Constitution. However, it includes nine narrow exceptions. Friedman Agnifilo’s motion argues that none of the exceptions apply, but she preemptively challenged CPL § 40.20(2)(b), “Each of the offenses as defined contains an element which is not an element of the other, and the statutory provisions defining such offenses are designed to prevent very different kinds of harm…” and 40.20(2)(f), “One of the offenses consists of a violation of a…provision of another jurisdiction, which offense has been prosecuted…and…been terminated by a court order…founded upon insufficiency of evidence to establish some element of such offense which is not an element of the other offense.”

In court for his guilty plea, Mangione for the first time described how he learned where UnitedHealthcare would hold its annual investor convergence in December 2024. He also learned who would attend. Mangione said that he printed a gun with a 3-D printer and affixed it with a silencer (suppressor). Defense attorney Friedman Agnifilo said that Mangione took full responsibility for Thompson’s death.

title: Latin American and Caribbean governments face pressure to restore women’s rights safeguards at Montevideo talks
content:
News

Latin American and Caribbean governments face pressure to restore women’s rights safeguards at Montevideo talks

Latin American and Caribbean governments convened Tuesday for a three-day UN conference on population and development, meeting amid what Amnesty International described as a regional rollback of protections for women, girls, and adolescents.

The Regional Conference on Population and Development (CRPD) will be held in the Uruguayan capital of Montevideo on August 18-20.

Ahead of the event, Amnesty International urged states to uphold their commitments under the Montevideo Consensus, one of the region’s most significant intergovernmental agreements on the rights of various population groups in the region, as defined by gender, ethnicity, age, and other factors.

Human rights advocates have long documented concerns regarding women’s health impacts in the region, owing to poor implementation of legal protections against gender based violence, femicide, child marriage, and restrictive reproductive rights.

Amnesty International indicated that the upcoming CRPD must prioritize gender justice and ensure that women’s rights groups are not dismantled and defunded, and that the Montevideo Consensus must be fully actualized in order to stop perpetuating the standard of institutionalized violence, coercion, and exploitation of women and girls.

“Amid a relentless wave of attacks on the rights of women, girls, and adolescents, the Montevideo Consensus must continue to be a roadmap for the protection of human rights and not a mere list of outstanding promises,” said Amnesty International’s Americas Director Ana Piquer. “Current challenges require concrete actions, adequate resources and effective accountability mechanisms.”

Despite the heightened aggression towards women’s rights organizations, groups and feminist movements such as UN Women and the Girls, Not Mothers campaign are working to bring light to and address the severity of the inequality faced by these populations. In recent years, UN Women has worked to enable women’s political participation and economic empowerment, as well as combat violence against women through the Belém do Pará Convention.

“Every woman, girl and adolescent must be able to make free and informed decisions regarding their bodies, every woman survivor of violence must have support and protection from the state, and every woman defender must be able to demand justice and equality without fear of reprisals,” said Piquer.

title: Reach Capital raises $265M Fund V to back AI founders building to ‘expand human potential’
author: Dominic-Madori Davis
content:
Reach Capital announced Tuesday the close of a $265 million Fund V. The thesis of the 11-year-old San Francisco firm is to back founders building AI applications that can “expand human potential,” Tony Wan, head of platform at Reach Capital, told TechCrunch. In practice, he added, that means looking at founders building across three areas: learning, health, and work.

“We believe AI should serve human flourishing, not replace it,” Wan said. The firm’s previous investments include Replit, ClassDojo, and Coral Care. 

The new fund will write checks of $1 million to $10 million, spanning pre-seed through Series A, into roughly 50 companies over the next three years. So far, no companies have been backed through Fund V.

Limited partners include Capricorn Investment Group, the Los Angeles Fire and Police Pensions, the LEGO Foundation, and College Board. Speaking to TechCrunch, general partner Jomayra Herrera said fundraising went smoothly and that the team was able to raise the new fund in less than six months. 

“The vast majority of our LPs doubled down, and we brought on a few new marquee LPs,” Herrera said. “We attribute this to LP interest in sector-focused boutique funds that focus on conviction-based investments.” 

Reach Capital’s new fund is noteworthy given the barbell shape the broader fundraising market has taken in recent years, with capital flowing overwhelmingly to giant, brand-name funds on one end and to sharply focused specialists on the other, with generalist firms in the middle struggling to get LPs’ attention.

Analysis by PitchBook and the National Venture Capital Association found that established firms captured more than 90% of the roughly $62 billion raised across U.S. VC funds through May of this year, leaving a smaller pool of first-time and mid-sized managers to compete for whatever’s left. Reach’s thesis, with over a decade of edtech and impact-investing, fits the mold of the kind of specialist fund LPs have remained open to funding.

The outfit previously raised $215 million for Fund IV in 2023 and $165 million for Fund III in 2021.

One of its most recent exits came in June, when Superhuman — the productivity platform formerly known as Grammarly — acquired GPTZero, the AI-detection startup co-founded by Princeton graduate Edward Tian. Terms weren’t disclosed, but GPTZero had grown to more than 19 million registered users and $30 million in annual recurring revenue on just $13.5 million raised, and Reach was one of several investors in the company, alongside Uncork Capital, Footwork, and Jack Altman’s Alt Capital.
